note: Amharic (am) is new to the library and not yet in language_seed.py (added from the admin).

Scripture authority is the Open Word Bible (OWB), Amharic, Balanced edition (CC0), bundled as library/data/bible/owb-am-b.json.gz and read offline (owb-am). Every Scripture quotation was re-quoted to it verbatim (founder decision, 2026-11-18: Amharic quotes OWB everywhere), replacing the 1962/2003 UBS New Testament wording and the Old Testament verses the first edition rendered in the 1962 register. The © UBS licence caveat of the first edition no longer applies to this work.

A `mined` row is a verbatim OWB span in that block: the whole verse, verses joined, the shortest contiguous span carrying the quoted clause, or exact OWB pieces joined with '…'; verbatim recitations without quote marks count. Two chapter titles quote Scripture and were re-quoted with it but carry no row, since rows are keyed by block index and a title has none: chapter 22 (Exodus 15:26, «እኔ የምፈውስህ እግዚአብሔር ነኝ») and chapter 32 (John 15:5, «እናንተ ቅርንጫፎቹ ናችሁ»). `self_rendered` rows (each with a `why`) are the places where Murray recasts, re-persons or argues from a wording OWB does not have.
Divine Healing (job #3655): 32 chapters translated by fan-out and reconciled as one book; Scripture re-quoted to OWB in one pass afterwards.

Editorial calls to check: Exodus 15:26, the book's refrain, now reads OWB's «እኔ የምፈውስህ እግዚአብሔር ነኝ» at every site, and Murray's answering prayer in chapter 22 echoes it («አዎን ጌታ ሆይ፣ የምትፈውሰኝ እግዚአብሔር አንተ ነህ»). 1 Corinthians 6:13's refrain 'The body is for the Lord' is OWB's «አካል ግን … ያለው ለጌታ ነው» / «ጌታም ለአካል ነው»; the chapter 9 and 10 titles (ሥጋ ለጌታ, ጌታ ለሥጋ) were left as headings. 'Thy will be done' (chapter 26) is Matthew 6:10's «ፈቃድህ በምድርም ይደረግ», the verse the chapter cites. Mark 9:23 in chapter 7: Murray quotes the KJV 'If thou canst believe' («ማመን ብትችል», kept, which the critical text OWB follows lacks) before the RV wording, which is OWB verbatim. Job 2:7 in OWB names 'the accuser' (ከሳሹ) where Murray's prose says Satan. John 11:40 is addressed to Martha (feminine) in OWB as in the 1962 text, while Murray applies it to a male believer. In chapter 11, Romans 4:19 is not quoted: OWB, like the 1962 text, reads that Abraham did consider his body, the reverse of the KJV sense the chapter argues from; the allusions stay prose.
